description: A floor, not a ground truth. Every statement here was checked by hand against the source text. Nothing claims the graph contains only these characters or only these relations — the work has roughly sixty named characters and several hundred defensible relationships, and asserting all of them would be asserting a guess. A pipeline satisfying this floor has not been proven correct; it has been proven not to be obviously wrong.

aliases_that_must_resolve.why: Four surface forms for the protagonist. A pipeline that splits them produces a graph with four half-connected centres.
The hard case. Unqualified 'Miss Bennet' denotes the eldest unmarried daughter — Jane, not Elizabeth. A pipeline that folds 'Miss Bennet' into Elizabeth will look plausible and be wrong throughout.

relations_that_must_exist.why: The principal axis of the work.

relations_that_must_not_exist.why: They share no scene in the work. An edge here indicates co-occurrence within a window being mistaken for interaction.
They never meet and are never associated. Same failure mode, larger distance.

notes: Chapter numbering follows the source text's own headings. Two chapters (13 and 14) carry their heading inside an illustration block rather than as a running head; any structural segmentation must handle both forms or it will misattribute their content to chapter 12.
Quotation matching is defined against whitespace-normalised text on both sides, because the source is hard-wrapped and quoted sentences span line breaks. See src/dramatis/text.py.
